summary: No findings. Trust boundary is the DOM (spec §8). A user who strips the disabled attribute and clicks still hits ActionBar.onClick's guard (model.enabled && action !== null, src/ui/table/ActionBar.tsx:18-20); idle buttons carry action null so nothing is submitted. Actions passed to onAct are the engine's own legalActions objects (not DOM-derived), so the UI cannot construct an arbitrary action. Defence in depth holds: useTableSession.act only applies on nextStep === 'user', applyUserAction re-checks the turn, and engine applyAction rejects out-of-turn or any action not matching legalActions by type and amount (src/engine/hand.ts:601-609). The fullBetTarget/BetContext refactor is behaviour-preserving and read-only over view data. Labels are built from a fixed vocabulary plus engine numbers and rendered as a React text child (no innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML), so they are plain text. No new dependencies, secrets, logging, randomness or network calls.
